thread:
zoe_pm: Dropping a focused UX thread for the routing policies editor. Two priorities: make ordering unmistakable, and make per-rule preview discoverable. Also: tighten validation copy so users know how to fix conflicts.
marc_design: New mock uploaded. Idea: left numeric badge for priority (editable), tiny drag handle on hover/focus, and a per-row 'Play' icon that opens a compact preview panel. Keeps the canvas clean.
tori_frontend: Numeric edit + drag sounds fine. Will add inline validation: when user types a duplicate or non-integer show: 'Must be a unique integer'. Also will add move up/down keyboard actions and aria announcements.
lee_research: From sessions people tried "run example" on the row; they liked seeing which rule would match. Make preview ephemeral and non-blocking. For copy, avoid vague phrases like "Rule conflict" 1: suggest: "Conflict with 'X' 1: both match the same input. Fix by reordering or editing conditions."
marc_design: Two copy options in the mock: Short helper: "Priority: lower numbers run first." Expanded helper: "Lower numbers are evaluated before higher numbers (1 runs before 2). If numbers match, top-to-bottom order is used."
tori_frontend: I'll wire aria: row role=listitem aria-posinset/aria-setsize, drag handle role=button aria-grabbed, and a status live region for reorder announcements. Preview runs will be debounced 400ms with spinner.
preview-bot: Deploy preview: https://deploy-previews.redwood.sh/1867-routing-preview-sandbox (includes initial keyboard moves and inline edit validation).
zoe_pm: Thanks! Marc drop final Figma link and exact ARIA strings here, then we'll schedule the eng review tomorrow."
